expectation: Granules in the cytoplasm, sometimes punctate, in cytotoxic CD8 T cells and NK cells. A minority population: single cells scattered in tumour stroma and infiltrates, denser in immune-rich regions. Most tumour cells stay negative.
observed: A: discrete yellow dots in every image, much denser in some (images 3, 7, 12), with faint diffuse haze in images 8 and 10. B and C: a few isolated bright cells against a dark background, not following nuclear density. D: one cell with clumpy cytoplasmic signal plus a few small granular neighbours.
why: A sparse set of distinct cells with granular cytoplasmic signal, whose density changes between images the way immune infiltration does, is what a GrzB stain should show.
notes: GrzB marks scattered single cells with granular cytoplasmic signal, densest in a few infiltrated images, while most tissue is dark. Two images have mild diffuse yellow haze, which is background and not the cellular signal.
